motion: an old hand lays a second dry split log beside the first one inside the stove firebox
an old hand turns the round iron damper handle a quarter turn on the stovepipe
a finger presses the test button of the plain white alarm and its green light starts to flash
the camera slowly moves closer to the metal plate on the back of the stove
thin wisps of grey ash dust drift up from the pail
the old hand turns the small round air control wheel slowly a little
the small shovel scoops grey ash out of the firebox
the hand pushes the paper twist gently into the kindling
faint heat shimmer rises along the stovepipe
a bead of water slowly runs down the wet cut face of the log
steam hisses out of the wet log end and bubbles spit
the flashlight beam moves slowly along the tar coated inside of the pipe
a few split logs roll off the top of the heap
the old hand turns the air control wheel a little to the left
a faint wisp of smoke curls behind the sooty glass
the gloved hand eases the stove door open a little and glowing coals brighten
the poker rakes the glowing coals forward
a few straws fall from the nest inside the pipe
a puff of grey smoke leans out of the open stove door into the room
a drop of dark tar slowly slides down the inside pipe wall
black creosote flakes fall from the brush onto the white cloth
the thread leans and flutters in the warm draft
the hand pushes the rolled towel tight along the bottom of the door
the hand presses the weatherstrip along the frame
the hand snaps the battery into the alarm
the hand lifts the dish towel away from the hot rail
